newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK SLOVNAFT SAYS SEEKS OIL SUPPLIER DIVERSITY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK SLOVNAFT SAYS SEEKS OIL SUPPLIER DIVERSITY.

text.p: Slovakia's sole oil refiner Slovnaft a.s. on Thursday said it was considering purchasing oil from the Middle East as part of an attempt to end its total reliance on Russian oil supplies.
Slovnaft spokesman Lubomir Zitnan told Reuters that company General Director Slavomir Hatina on Thursday morning left for a visit to United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Kuwait.
"One part of his visit will be talks on possible future purchase of their oil," Zitnan said.
But he added that these talks will be in the stage of preliminary negotiations.
Slovakia currently relies on oil supplies from Russia which are imported through the Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline via Ukraine.
Middle East oil could be sent to Slovakia through the Adria pipeline, which is now fully operational after its temporary closure due to the war in former Yugoslavia.
Zitnan said, however, that Slovnaft still considered Russian oil as the most favourable source.

At the beginning of the year then Slovak foreign minister Juraj Schenk discussed possible oil deals with UAE and Kuwait. But he said the main obstacle for importing gulf oil would be its price, higher due to transport costs.
The talks were only general and Schenk said concrete details of possible deals would be subject to further negotiations between experts from all of the countries involved.
It was not known whether Hatina's visit was part of this plan.
Slovakia has been considering other oil sources after supplies through the Druzhba pipeline were suspended due to disputes over transfer fees between Russia and Ukraine for the second year running.
